newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges soar on refinery glitch.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges soar on refinery glitch.

text.p: NWE high sulphur fuel barges soared on Tuesday despite poor bunker demand as Shell bought product because of an unspecified problem at their refinery in Rotterdam, traders said.
High sulphur barges traded at $92 fob ARA, then jumped to trade as high as $97, $98 and $99.
But high sulphur cargoes failed to move far upwards amid a continuation of good cargo and storage supply in the region and a perception that the refinery problem would be short-lived.
Utilities saw offers little changed at around $97 cif NWE. "There is plenty of material around," one regular buyer said.
Low sulphur fuel oil was little changed in the face of continued Italian indifference to a well-supplied cargo market.
A UK refiner on Friday received low sulphur from a refinery in Scandinavia, in exchange for a cargo out of southern Spain which will go to the Scandinavian refinery's Italian affiliate.
Traders did not expect new Italian buying because of congestion in Italy which meant ENEL would not be in a position to receive vessels before the last week of the month.
But underlying this short term glitch was a bearish demand picture -- data emerged that Italy's electricity consumption rate fell by 0.8 percent in January compared to last year.
